[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Large Language Models (LLMs) and Fine-Tuning"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Introduction to LLMs and Fine-Tuning"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Large Language Models (LLMs) are deep learning architectures trained on massive corpora of text data. While base models possess general linguistic capabilities and broad knowledge, fine-tuning allows developers to adapt these models to specific domains, tasks, or alignment criteria using targeted datasets."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Fine-Tuning Paradigms"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Full Fine-Tuning: Updates all parameters of the pre-trained model. Highly resource-intensive and requires significant GPU memory."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT): Freezes the base model weights and trains a small subset of parameters, drastically reducing computational overhead."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA): A popular PEFT method that injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into the transformer layers."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementing LoRA Fine-Tuning with Python"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a practical example using the Hugging Face ecosystem (transformers, peft, and trl) to fine-tune an LLM efficiently."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, TrainingArguments
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
import torch

model_id = "meta-llama/Llama-3-8b"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)

lora_config = LoraConfig(
    r=16,
    lora_alpha=32,
    target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"],
    lora_dropout=0.05,
    bias="none",
    task_type="CAUSAL_LM"
)

model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)
model.print_trainable_parameters()"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Training Configuration and Execution"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once the PEFT model is initialized, you must configure the training arguments using the TrainingArguments class and run the SFTTrainer from the TRL library for supervised fine-tuning."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from trl import SFTTrainer

training_args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="./results",
    per_device_train_batch_size=4,
    gradient_accumulation_steps=4,
    learning_rate=2e-4,
    logging_steps=10,
    num_train_epochs=3,
    fp16=True,
    optim="adamw_torch"
)

trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model=model,
    train_dataset=dataset,
    dataset_text_field="text",
    max_seq_length=512,
    args=training_args,
)

trainer.train()"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Best Practices for Production"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Data Quality: Ensure your training data is clean, diverse, and representative of the target inference distribution."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Evaluation: Utilize benchmarks and human evaluation (RLHF) to check for catastrophic forgetting and hallucination rates."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Quantization: Combine LoRA with 4-bit quantization (QLoRA) to fine-tune massive models on consumer-grade hardware."}]
